speaker.instructions: Who wrote reviewer_comment? Judge from its content together with commenter_is_change_author and commenter_account. Code review bots and AI review assistants count as automation even when they write like a person.

criteria.reviewer: A person reviewing someone else's change and giving feedback on it
criteria.author: The change's own author or co-author annotating, explaining or asking about their own change
criteria.automation: Output of a bot, CI system, linter or AI review assistant, or a person only typing a bot command such as /lgtm, @bors r+, /test, please test

criteria.finding: States that something in the change is wrong, broken, missing or risky and should be fixed
criteria.suggestion: Proposes a better alternative or improvement without claiming the current code is wrong
criteria.question: Asks for clarification, rationale or information without asserting a problem
criteria.nit: Trivial: typo, formatting, whitespace, wording or minor naming preference
criteria.ack: Approval, thanks, LGTM, Reviewed-by or agreement with no request
criteria.process: CI, test runs, labels, merging, backports, scheduling or other discussion not about the code itself

topic.instructions: Which aspect of the code does reviewer_comment concern? Pick the most specific one.

criteria.logic: Incorrect logic or result: wrong condition, off-by-one, wrong value, missed case in control flow
criteria.error_handling: Failure paths, error propagation, input validation, edge or boundary inputs, null or empty cases
criteria.concurrency: Races, locking, atomics, memory ordering, async, cancellation, reentrancy, thread safety
criteria.memory_resources: Object lifetime, ownership, leaks, use-after-free, buffer or integer overflow, unsafe code, resource cleanup
criteria.security: Trust boundaries, untrusted input, injection, crypto misuse, privilege, denial of service, information leaks
criteria.performance: Complexity, allocations, hot paths, caching, unnecessary work, memory footprint
criteria.api_compat: Public interface or behaviour visible to users or callers, semantics, backward or ABI compatibility, deprecation
criteria.design: Architecture, abstraction, where code belongs, layering, duplication, or a simpler overall approach
criteria.tests: Missing, weak or incorrect tests, coverage of cases, test reliability
criteria.readability: Clarity, naming, needed code comments, structure, dead code, simplifying code without changing behaviour
criteria.docs: Documentation, commit message, changelog, user-facing messages
criteria.build_platform: Build system, portability, platform or architecture differences, configuration, dependencies
criteria.none: Not about the code (thanks, process, CI)

depth.instructions: How much understanding did writing reviewer_comment require?
criteria: Surface: visible at a glance, such as typos, formatting or naming taste
Local: requires careful reading of the changed lines themselves
Contextual: requires knowledge of surrounding code, callers, project conventions or history beyond the shown lines
Deep: requires system-level knowledge such as invariants, concurrency or memory models, hardware, specifications, or consequences far from the change

severity.instructions: If reviewer_comment is right and the code had shipped unchanged, how bad would the consequence be?
criteria: Maintainability cost: harder to read, change or debug later
Wrong behaviour in some cases, a performance regression, or a misleading interface
Crash, data loss or corruption, security hole, or widespread breakage

outcome.instructions: What happened to the point raised in reviewer_comment? Use replies (each tagged with the speaker's role) and signals: outdated means the commented code changed after the comment; resolved means the thread was marked resolved; later_version means the author posted a new version of the patch.

criteria.accepted: The author agreed and changed the code or committed to change it
criteria.explained: The author or others answered or explained, and the point was settled without a change
criteria.rejected: The author disagreed or declined and the code stayed as it was
criteria.deferred: Agreed but left for a follow-up change
criteria.unknown: No reply and no signal that decides it

concrete.instructions: Does reviewer_comment name a concrete mechanism, scenario, input, sequence of events or counterexample, rather than a vague concern or preference?

criteria.false: Vague, general or a matter of preference

proposes_fix.instructions: Does reviewer_comment propose a specific fix, code or alternative?

criteria.true: Gives a specific fix, code suggestion or alternative

beyond_diff.instructions: Does reviewer_comment rely on code, callers, history, specifications or behaviour outside the code shown in code_context?

criteria.true: Draws on knowledge beyond the shown code
criteria.false: Based only on the shown code
